videos.name: Piri Reis
videos.title: Did Someone Map Antarctica Before the Ice?
videos.description:
How many of us are really sure what's in Antarctica? The Piri Reis map of 1513 is famous for showing it before the ice. Here is what the map, and Piri Reis's own notes, actually say.

Drawn by the Ottoman admiral Piri Reis at Gallipoli in 1513 and rediscovered in Topkapı Palace in 1929, the map was later claimed to show an ice-free Antarctica mapped by a lost civilization. The ice is millions of years older than that, and historians read the southern coast as South America bent east to fit the gazelle skin. The real secret is in the margins: Piri Reis says he used about twenty source maps, one of them drawn by Columbus, whose own map has never been found.

Someone lived in Antarctica before the ice: REAL or MYTH? Tell me in the comments.

Sources
- Piri Reis map, Gallipoli, 1513 (Topkapı Palace Library, Istanbul); rediscovered in 1929
- The map's marginal notes, translated by Yusuf Akçura (Türk Tarih Kurumu, 1935)
- Charles Hapgood, Maps of the Ancient Sea Kings (1966); Erich von Däniken, Chariots of the Gods? (1968)
- Gregory C. McIntosh, The Piri Reis Map of 1513 (University of Georgia Press, 2000)
- Antarctic ice sheet: about 34 million years old; Antarctica first sighted in January 1820

videos.name: Salem
videos.title: Everything You Know About the Salem Witches Is Wrong
videos.description:
Not one witch was burned in Salem in 1692. So what really happened to the 20 people who died?

The legend says Salem burned its witches. The court records say otherwise: 19 hanged, one man crushed under stones, and the last name cleared in 2022. Real or myth? Tell me in the comments.

videos.name: Battle of Ankara
videos.title: The Sultan Betrayed by His Own Army | Battle of Ankara 1402 (Timur vs Bayezid)
videos.description:
He had never lost a war. By sunset, he was in chains, betrayed by his own army.

July 28, 1402. On a plain near Ankara, the two most feared rulers of their age met in battle: Timur (Tamerlane), the conqueror who built towers of skulls, and Ottoman Sultan Bayezid "the Thunderbolt", the man who crushed the Crusaders at Nicopolis.

It started with insulting letters, including one of the gravest insults a ruler could put in writing. It ended with a dammed river, Christian knights fighting to the last for the sultan, a secret message to the Tatar cavalry… and a legend of an iron cage.

How could an empire that never lost… lose everything in a single day? Who do you think was the greater commander, Timur or Bayezid? Tell me in the comments.

videos.name: Noah's Ark
videos.title: The Mistake Everyone Makes About Noah's Ark #shorts #bible
videos.description:
The Bible never says Noah's Ark landed on Mount Ararat. Not once.

Genesis 8:4 says only "the mountains of Ararat", and Ararat was a kingdom, Urartu, around Lake Van. The oldest Jewish translation, the Targum Onkelos, says the mountains of Qardu. The Babylonian priest Berossus, as quoted by Josephus, placed the ship's remains in the Gordyaean mountains. The Quran names al-Judi. Many scholars place all three around Mount Cudi in southeastern Turkey.

So... Ararat or Cudi? Or do you think Noah's Ark really existed? Comment REAL or MYTH.
Subscribe to Unsealed History for more history mysteries, told from the sources.

Sources: Genesis 8:4; Targum Onkelos, Genesis 8:4; Berossus via Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews I.93; Quran, Surah Hud 11:44.

videos.name: Atlantis
videos.title: Atlantis Was Never Found… So Where Did the Story Come From? #shorts
videos.description:
Everyone knows Atlantis. Almost no one knows where the story comes from.

There is no ancient map, no ruins, no inscription. The whole legend traces back to one man: Plato, writing around 360 BC in the Timaeus and the Critias. An Egyptian priest told it to Solon, Solon passed it down for generations, and it reached Plato's character Critias.

Real, or the greatest story ever told? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe to Unsealed History for more history mysteries, told from the sources.

Sources: Plato, Timaeus 20d–25d and Critias (c. 360 BC).
Images: Athanasius Kircher, map of Atlantis (Mundus Subterraneus, 1678); Gustave Doré, The Deluge; busts of Plato and Solon (public domain, Wikimedia Commons).
